triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

First touch (R1198, 16:0xZ): **p2 · domain:ui** → `pm:queue`.

Theme: zh-CN customers. This card holds two items. (1) Per-position or per-role view audiences are a feature request with no break, so p2. (2) A console-created view answering 403 when customized in Studio is a bug. If its cause is separate, the claiming dev splits (2) out on its own card at p1.

repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUgZpbKcVYFC7iXgMu

Split · 2026-11-19T17:05Z: item 2 (a console-created view answering 403 "declares an override of …, which ships no view named …" when customized in Studio) now lives on #35600 (p1, as the first touch 6953426292 directed). The 403 is the server's `shipsNoSuchItemMessage` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts:1142-1172`) answering a Customize body that declares `overrides` of a base which does not ship that view; nothing on that path touches item 1.

**This card keeps item 1 only**: a view gets an optional audience (positions, roles or permission sets) set by the administrator. That is a Feature that reaches the spec's view shape and a visibility boundary, so it owes a scope review before any dispatch. It stays `pm:queue`; area b1-U does not claim it.

repo:objectstack#7 · os-alice · session_011y7As5bdhV5T4N9vpjmZzH

## 维护者速读

- 问题:管理员在控制台新建的列表视图,发布后凡是能读这个对象的人都看得见;管理员没法在界面上指定「只给业务员看」「只给经理看」。今天有一家中文客户部署卡在这里,此前一个合同管理应用也提过同样的需求(一个对象上十一个视图、四类人)。
- 选项:A 在视图上直接勾选岗位或角色,等于平台另造第二套「谁能看」规则,约三到四个 PR,还要改一份已定的架构决定;B 平台早已有、而且由服务器强制执行的「所需权限」受众门,只是控制台和设计器里没有填写入口,把入口补上,挑选时顺带显示哪些岗位会看到,约两个 PR;C 暂不做,只写一份操作说明。
- 推荐 B:谁能看视图的规则已经定过、也已在服务器生效,缺的只是管理员能点的入口,不必再造第二套规则。
- 不定会怎样:管理员要按岗位分视图,只能找开发商改源码,客户「管理员自己配、不找厂商」的目标落空。

---

## English analysis (for reviewers and agents)

<sub>Card body and both comments (triage 6953426292, split by os-sales) re-read at 2026-11-23T10:28Z; corpus measured at `origin/main` 3cf6a44b.</sub>

### Background

The card now holds item 1 only: an administrator wants to give a published list view an audience (positions, roles or permission sets) so that only that audience sees it. Item 2, the Studio 403, moved to #35600 and is not discussed here. The triage and split comments call item 1 "a Feature that reaches the spec's view shape and a visibility boundary". **The first half of that premise does not hold.** The view shape already carries an audience key, and the server enforces it:

- `ListViewSchema.requiredPermissions` is declared at `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:3697-3708`. Its describe is `packages/spec/src/ui/audience-required-permissions.ts:45-53`. It was added by ruling of record 6095014058 on #22611 (letter A, maintainer 「同意」), landed in PR #22665 (+349/−5, 19 files).
- The `/meta` read gate enforces it. `holdsRequiredPermissions` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:797-799`) requires every named capability, and `filterViewForUser` (`:901-919`) and `pruneListViewRecord` (`:865-872`) withhold or prune list views the caller does not hold. This landed in PR #22731 (+1267/−165, 27 files). The liveness row `packages/spec/liveness/view.json:175-180` reads `live`.
- The key is declared on the list-view shape, so it reaches every door the console writes through: a view item's `config` and the flattened overlay arm (`view.zod.ts:3701-3707`).
- Positions already reach capabilities. A position confers capability only through the permission sets it names (`packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts:62-68`, `:97-113`). A permission set grants capabilities through free `systemPermissions` tags, editable in Setup (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.form.ts:67`). The docs already teach "one capability, granted to each audience's set" (`content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx:165-197`).

**What is actually missing is an authoring surface.** An administrator has no control anywhere in the console or Studio for a list view's audience:

- The view metadata form's "Navigation & sharing" section is described as "Where this view appears and who can see it." It offers only `navigation` and `sharing.lockedBy` (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.form.ts:279-317`). `requiredPermissions` has 0 occurrences in `view.form.ts` and in `dashboard.form.ts`. By contrast, `app.form.ts:102` offers `requiredPermissions` as a `string-tags` row.
- The console's 新建视图 dialog offers only `personal | shared` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/CreateViewDialog.tsx:1082`, `:1160`). Its shared hint says "Shared views are seen by everyone who can see this list" (`:1338`), and the file has 0 occurrences of `requiredPermissions`.
- The Studio list-view inspector (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectListViewInspector.tsx`) and the console view-config utilities (`ui/packages/plugin-view/src/config/view-config-utils.ts`) also have 0 occurrences.

So today only source code (an `*.view.ts` file) can set the gate. That is exactly the 「不找厂商」 requirement the card reports as unmet.

Governing text: ADR-0066 "The three-way separation (principle)", `docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md:14-21`: "a resource declares the capability it requires (a stable contract); the capability and its assignment are dynamic, admin-maintained records. A resource never bakes 'who' — only 'what is required'." Ruling of record 6095014058 on #22611 (letter A): "`ListViewSchema` and `DashboardSchema` each gain `requiredPermissions` with the same shape and semantics as the app, navigation-item, action … and record-block keys", "A creates no second audience mechanism". Spec docblock: `packages/spec/src/ui/audience-required-permissions.ts:3-38` (all-of, no any-of form, enforced by the server). `rg -n "never bakes" docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md` → 1 hit (line 21).

### Protocol declaration

- B changes no protocol. It adds no key, value or export. It adds a form row in `packages/spec/src/ui/view.form.ts` / `dashboard.form.ts` (authoring-form metadata, not schema) and console controls.
- A changes protocol: a new authorable key on `ListViewSchema` plus a new read-gate arm. Because it bakes "who" into a resource, it also needs an amendment to ADR-0066, which is Tier H.
- C changes nothing.

### Premises (each with its re-check)

1. P1: the list view carries the audience key. Re-check: `rg -n "requiredPermissions: z.array" packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` → `:3708`.
2. P2: the server enforces it. Re-check: `rg -n -A2 '"requiredPermissions"' packages/spec/liveness/view.json` → `"status": "live"`.
3. P3: no authoring form offers it for a view or a dashboard. Re-check: `rg -c requiredPermissions packages/spec/src/ui/view.form.ts packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.form.ts` → no output (0 each). The app form does offer it: `rg -n requiredPermissions packages/spec/src/ui/app.form.ts` → `:102`.
4. P4: no console or Studio control sets it. Re-check: `rg -c requiredPermissions ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/CreateViewDialog.tsx ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectListViewInspector.tsx ui/packages/plugin-view/src` → no output.
5. P5: a position reaches a capability only through its permission sets. Re-check: `rg -n "capability reaches a position" packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts` → `:64`.
6. P6: no example app gates a list view. Re-check: `rg -n requiredPermissions examples/*/src --include=*.view.ts`. Expected: only the bulk-action defs at `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/project.view.ts:144,152` and a comment at `field-zoo.view.ts:71`, and no list-level key.

### The concrete question

The rule for who sees a list view is already ruled and enforced: a capability on the view, and positions holding it through permission sets. Should the platform add a second, direct "positions / roles on the view" mechanism, give administrators a control for the existing one, or leave it source-only for now?

### Options

| Option | What is done | What the customer sees | Effort (lane · PRs · measured precedent) |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** Per-view principal audience | New `audience: { positions?, permissionSets? }` key (or similar) on `ListViewSchema` and `DashboardSchema`. A new read-gate arm resolves the caller's positions and sets. Console picker. ADR-0066 amended. | Admin ticks 「业务员」「经理」 directly on the view. | spec + rest + ui + ADR (Tier H) · 3–4 PRs · about the size of the existing key: #22665 (+349/−5) + #22731 (+1267/−165) + an inspector control like #26977 (+804/−126), so roughly 2,400+ lines plus the ADR edit |
| **B** Author the existing gate from the console | The `navigation_sharing` section of `view.form.ts` (and `dashboard.form.ts`) gains a `requiredPermissions` row, same widget as `app.form.ts:102`. 新建视图 (shared scope) and the Studio list-view inspector gain a "Who sees this view" picker over known capabilities that shows, read-only, which positions hold each one. The shared hint is corrected. `capabilities.mdx` gains the administrator recipe. | Admin picks 「客户视图·业务员」 (a capability granted to the 业务员 position's set) and sees "业务员 will see this view". Others no longer see it in the switcher, and opening it by URL is refused. | spec + ui · 2 PRs · form rows: #20405 (+182/−6, 9 files, five rows including object `requiredPermissions`). Inspector control: #26977 (+804/−126, 13 files). Roughly 600–1,000 lines. |
| **C** Defer, document only | `capabilities.mdx` gains a recipe saying "set `requiredPermissions` on the view in source". | Nothing changes in the console. The administrator still asks the vendor. | docs · 1 PR · no precedent measured, tens of lines |

**What each option means for the business**

- A: like giving every filing cabinet its own guest list, beside the badge system the building already runs.
- B: the building already checks badges at this door. B gives the receptionist the screen to choose which badge opens it.
- C: the door can be locked, but only the locksmith can set it.

### Four axes, per option (business stance)

**① Long-term soundness (weight ≥50%).** Two-year end state: one audience vocabulary across every entry the platform serves (app, navigation item, action, record block, list view, dashboard). A resource names the capability it needs, administrators decide who holds it in Setup, and every authoring surface, console included, can pick it. This is the Salesforce custom-permission model: a custom permission is assigned through permission sets and permission set groups and required by apps, tabs and Lightning page components. It is also the one the ADR-0066 three-way separation rules.

- Salesforce list views can also be shared directly with public groups and roles. That is a second, principal-based mechanism, and ADR-0066 (`:21`) and ruling 6095014058 ("creates no second audience mechanism") explicitly declined it here.
- **B** completes the one mechanism and adds no special case. It shrinks contract growth to zero: the key is already paid for (declared, enforced, live).
- **A** creates a second audience mechanism on two entry types only. A list view would then answer "who" two ways (capability and principals), while apps, actions and blocks answer it one way. Every reader of view audiences, and every future entry type, then has to choose between the two. It also contradicts governing text, so it cannot be taken without an ADR-0066 amendment.
- **C** leaves an enforced capability unreachable from the product's own administration surface. That is a durable gap, not a contract problem.

**② Actual business need (measured pull).**

- Today: the reporting zh-CN deployment, measured in a browser on 18.5.0 (card body, item 1). Earlier: the hotclm administrator in #22611 ("eleven views and four audiences on one object", ruling 6095014058).
- In-repo: 0 example list views use the gate (P6), so all measured pull comes from deployments, and all of it asks for an administrator, not a developer, to set the audience.
- A and B both meet the need. B meets it with one more step for the administrator: the capability has to exist and be granted to the position's set. That step is done once per audience in Setup, which already exists (`permission.form.ts:67`).
- C leaves both deployments' requirement unmet.

**③ AI-error resistance (who sees what when it goes wrong).**

- **B**'s console picker is a closed list of capabilities the environment knows, so an administrator, or an AI driving the console, cannot type a name that matches nothing. Source authoring keeps today's lint warning (`packages/lint/src/validate-capability-references.ts:45`).
- When the gate is wrong, the failure is loud and narrow. A non-holder is refused by name with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (`audience-required-permissions.ts:27-31`). The one quiet failure is already recorded: a misspelled name hides the view from everyone except object editors (`liveness/view.json:178`). The closed picker removes that case from the console path.
- **A** gives an AI two plausible spellings for the same intent (capability or principal list), so it will pick the wrong one on some entries. A position name that resolves to nothing would hide the view from that audience with no message: a silent loss.
- **C** keeps AI-authored source unchanged and moves the error to vendor hand-edits.

**④ Startup stage, no scope creep.**

- **B** declares nothing new and adds no gate. It wires an authoring surface to a key the platform already maintains, which finishes a declared capability rather than expanding one.
- **A** adds a permanent key on two schemas, a second resolver arm, and an ADR amendment. Each of those is a lasting obligation.
- **C** costs nothing now, but leaves a shipped, enforced capability that administrators cannot reach.

os-decision-facets
- ① Long-term soundness: B shrinks special cases (no new key, one audience mechanism across all entries, per ADR-0066 :14-21); A grows a second, principal-based mechanism on two entry types and conflicts with governing text; C leaves an enforced key administrator-unreachable.
- ② Actual business pull: two named deployments (this card's zh-CN deployment, measured on 18.5.0; hotclm via #22611); 0 in-repo example list views use the gate; both deployments ask for administrator-set audiences, which A and B meet and C does not.
- ③ AI-error resistance: B is a closed capability picker, and a wrong gate is refused loudly by name (403); A has two spellings for one intent, and an unresolved position name silently hides the view; C is unchanged.
- ④ No scope creep: B declares no key and adds no gate (UI over a live key); A adds a permanent key, a resolver arm and a Tier-H ADR edit; C costs zero but strands a shipped capability.
Prior rulings read: requiredPermissions,audience,systemPermissions,capability → 65 hits (narrowed run); views,list,view,assigned,positions,roles,created,console,403s,customized,studio → 139 hits (title run); ADR-0066 D1, ADR-0066 D3, ADR-0066 D4, ADR-0090 D9, ADR-0068 D4, ADR-0131 D13; ruling 6095014058 (#22611, letter A); #28971 letter C (personal views are a user-owned record, not view metadata, `view.zod.ts:6056-6064`); thread: none (0 rulings among the card's 2 comments)

### Recommendation: B

- B completes the one audience mechanism the platform already rules and enforces, and adds no key. It is the only option that meets the measured administrator-set need without a second "who" vocabulary.
- **Not A:** it creates a second audience mechanism the governing text forbids, at about 2.4× B's effort. ① already separates A and B, so the ≥3× rule does not apply.
- **Not C:** both measured deployments stay blocked on the vendor, for a gap that costs about two PRs to close.

Self-check: 只看①选 B;②③④ 是否翻转:否。

**Confidence gaps (stated, not grounds for another option):**

- Not measured: whether the console can already read the environment's capability catalog (registry `capability` items per `packages/spec/src/security/capabilities.ts:13-14`, plus the free `systemPermissions` strings in served permission sets) and the position → permission-set map for the read-only "who will see it" preview. If neither read is served to the console, B's UI PR also needs one read, which is the third-tier premise below.
- Not measured: whether Studio's raw-JSON editor (if any) already lets an administrator type the key. That would lessen C's harm but would not meet 「不找厂商」 for a business administrator.
- Not measured: the 403 behaviour a gated view shows its own creator when they do not hold the capability. The read gate exempts callers who may edit the object (`audience-required-permissions.ts:31-34`), so an administrator should keep seeing it.

### After the ruling (execution, so the maintainer rules direction only)

Third-tier premise the dispatch order carries:

- (a) P1–P4 still hold.
- (b) A console write body carrying `requiredPermissions` on a shared view is kept by the save door (the shape claim at `view.zod.ts:3701-3707`). The dev proves this with one round-trip test before building UI.
- ⛔ If (b) fails (the door strips or refuses it), the dev reports a fork. The dev does not widen the save door, and does not fall back to C or to a console-only flag.

Steps:

1. **spec PR** (`domain:spec`): add a `requiredPermissions` row to the `navigation_sharing` section of `packages/spec/src/ui/view.form.ts`, with help text taken from `AUDIENCE_REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS_DESCRIPTION`, and the matching row in `dashboard.form.ts`. Add the i18n catalog keys and the zh-CN label 「所需权限」 in the `view` section of `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/metadata-form-zh-cn.ts` (the label already exists in five other sections, e.g. `:139`). The spec release lands before the UI consumes it (the installation-surface ordering of ruling 6095014058).
2. **ui PR** (`domain:ui`):
   - Add an optional "Who sees this view" picker to 新建视图 for the `shared` scope and to the Studio list-view inspector.
   - The picker offers only capabilities the environment knows (closed list) and shows, read-only, the positions that hold each one.
   - The view surface never writes permission sets or positions. Granting stays in Setup.
   - Correct the shared hint at `CreateViewDialog.tsx:1338` so it no longer claims everyone sees a gated view.
3. **docs** (same ui PR or the spec PR): add the administrator recipe to `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`: create the capability in a permission set, attach the set to the positions, pick it on the view.
4. No new gate, no new key, no any-of form (ruled out by 6095014058, letter B not taken).

Card state on ruling: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. The body's item 1 is rewritten to "author the existing list-view / dashboard audience gate from the console and Studio". `domain:ui` stays and `domain:spec` is added for the form row. `priority:p2` is unchanged.

### Related

- #22611 (the ruling that created the key)
- #22665 (spec half, +349/−5)
- #22731 (rest gate, +1267/−165)
- #35600 (item 2, split out)
- #28971 (personal named views ruling)
- #32587 (skills teaching `requiredPermissions`, closed)
- #20405 (form-row precedent)
- #26977 (inspector-control precedent)

repo:objectstack#7 · os-alice · session_011y7As7yb6MicBqUUEzgjGB

Ruling: #34908 · letter B · maintainer 「B 给已有权限门补入口」 2026-11-23T14:15Z

The maintainer (os-alice) picked **B** on the project decision card at 2026-11-23T12:03:56Z, answering 「列表视图按岗位可见,选哪种做法?」 against the three options of the analysis in 7098042572. The tapped option reads, verbatim: 「B 给已有权限门补入口 — 控制台和设计器加「谁能看此视图」选择,并显示哪些岗位会看到;不改协议,约2个PR。」

**What is ruled (direction only):** a list view's (and a dashboard's) audience stays the existing, server-enforced `requiredPermissions` gate. The platform adds administrator authoring surfaces for it in the console and Studio. It does **not** add a second, principal-based audience key (A not taken), and it does not defer to a source-only recipe (C not taken).

**Execution:** exactly as the "After the ruling" section of 7098042572 states, including its third-tier premise (a)/(b) and the ⛔ fork rule if the save door strips or refuses `requiredPermissions`:

1. spec PR (`domain:spec`): `requiredPermissions` row in the `navigation_sharing` section of `view.form.ts`, matching row in `dashboard.form.ts`, i18n keys and the zh-CN label 「所需权限」.
2. ui PR (`domain:ui`): optional "Who sees this view" picker in 新建视图 (shared scope) and the Studio list-view inspector, closed list of known capabilities, read-only preview of the positions holding each; the shared hint at `CreateViewDialog.tsx` corrected. Granting stays in Setup.
3. docs: the administrator recipe in `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`.
4. No new key, no new gate, no any-of form.

**Card state:** `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:spec` added beside `domain:ui`; `priority:p2` and `area:build` unchanged. Item 1 of the body reads, from this ruling on: "author the existing list-view / dashboard audience gate from the console and Studio". Contract-review tier carries to dispatch.
